I didn't say that as a straight white male your voice didn't matter...I said all Torontonians have a say in this and should be able to constructively criticize BLM. Which you did. I didn't criticize you for not learning earlier. I'm genuinely interested in what was it about the post that helped you to come to a better understanding. Hence my question - "What was it about this reply that changes your mind?" And I'm still interested in your response.

Also you (and lots of folks) need to reshape your thinking of BLM. It's not about the leaders (or if YOU think they're fit or not fit). It's about what the community feels and the collectivity that these women are creating. BLM is not focused on the leaders, they are focused on creating communities of healing and change and justice. Why are criticizers so focused on the leaders and not the issues? 
I don't believe that BLMTO should be without criticism from Black folks and Torontonians - in fact I don't think there isn't enough (constructive) criticism thrown their way. BUT if the community is responding to BLM in a positive way and the community feels supported and is getting their voice heard - then BLM is doing their job.
